今天的主题：广告、消费和购物心理。这组词对 G 类特别实用：写作 Task 2 常考「广告对消费者好还是坏」「该不该禁止面向儿童的广告」；口语 Part 1 的 Shopping、Advertisements，Part 3 的 consumer society 都能直接用；G 类阅读里的商店促销、退换货规定也常出现 purchase、promote、discount 这类词。

例句

  • Many companies pay famous athletes to endorse their products.（很多公司花钱请著名运动员给产品代言。）
  • Advertisers try to persuade consumers that they need things they don't really need.（广告商试图说服消费者，让他们觉得自己需要其实并不需要的东西。）
  • Some shoppers make an impulse purchase when they see a big discount.（有些顾客看到大折扣就会冲动消费。）
  • People tend to trust a credible expert more than an ordinary advert.（人们往往更相信可信的专家，而不是普通广告。）
  • A large proportion of young people are influenced by what they see on social media.（很大一部分年轻人会被社交媒体上看到的内容影响。）

过关标准：遮住中文看英文，能说出 22 个以上的意思，再挑 5 个自己造句（试试用 persuade、consumer、impulse 写一句你对广告的看法，Task 2 和口语 Part 3 都能直接用）。

BBC 6 Minute English：How advertisers make us spend money（广告商怎样让我们花钱）。这集讲为什么名人代言管用（它是一种思维捷径），为什么快餐店装了触屏点餐机以后大家花得更多（不怕被店员评判，更容易被追加销售），还有联合国在突尼斯拍电视剧鼓励大家一起吃饭。全集只有两位主持人和三段短录音，内容贴近日常购物，很适合精听。音频和原文都已经放在页面里，不用打开 BBC 网站。

  1. 先把上面的听前生词过一遍，听不太懂可以先读懂原文再听。
  2. 第一遍不看文字，只听大意，回答开头的问题：认为人会对小小的提示做出反应的理论叫什么？a) push theory b) pull theory c) nudge theory。顺便听出：用触屏点餐后每单消费大约增加多少？联合国世界粮食计划署在哪个国家拍了电视剧？
  3. 第二遍点开下面的原文精听，听不出的地方暂停、倒回去并标出来。Ben Jones、Dean Ward 和 Takwa Khelifi 三段是真实录音，语速稍快，多听几遍，尤其是 Dean 讲 feeling judged 和 upsell 那段。
  4. 第三遍挑 Dean 那段（"So, would you like extra fries? Would you like to go large?..."）跟读，模仿语调和连读。
  5. 记住 6 个表达：mental shortcut（思维捷径）、feel judged（觉得被评判）、upsell（追加销售）、basket spend（客单价，单次消费额）、think outside the box（跳出框框思考）、model behaviour（示范行为让人模仿）。
点开看原文（难词带中文，点虚线词显示）
💡 点击或悬停虚线词看中文；点击说话人名字可单独切换该段翻译

Pippa：Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Pippa.

Pippa：大家好，这里是 BBC 学习英语的《六分钟英语》。我是皮帕。

Phil：And I'm Phil. What's the last thing you bought and why did you buy it?

Phil：我是菲尔。你最近买的一样东西是什么？为什么买它？

Pippa：I bought a new pair of headphones recently because my old ones broke, and I did lots of research to try and find a good pair. How about you?

Pippa：我最近买了一副新耳机，因为旧的坏了，我做了很多功课想挑一副好的。你呢？

Phil：I bought a soft drink软饮料，汽水 on the way to work this morning. It might be because I saw someone I like promoting it in an advert广告. We call this a celebrity名人 endorsement代言. But why do they work? Let's start by hearing from Ben Jones, a behavioural行为的 research expert, speaking to BBC World Service programme Business Daily.

Phil：我今天早上上班路上买了一瓶汽水。可能是因为我在广告里看到一个我喜欢的人在推销它。这叫名人代言。可代言为什么管用呢？我们先听听行为研究专家本·琼斯在 BBC 国际频道节目《每日商业》里怎么说。

Ben Jones：When we're unsure, we don't know what to do, it's kind of easy to follow the lead of跟着……走，效仿 those who we think are credible可信的 or knowledgeable懂行的，知识渊博的. It's a mental shortcut思维捷径. It's something that helps us navigate应对，摸索着度过 uncertain不确定的 times or make quick choices. We start doing that from an early age. Our parents… for some people, it's about our teachers – you know, these people who help us learn and make sense of the world理解世界. And some businesses can draw on利用，借助 this through things like endorsements代言 – you know, dentists recommending toothpaste, athletes endorsing代言 sportswear运动服.

Ben Jones：当我们拿不准、不知道该怎么做的时候，跟着那些我们觉得可信或懂行的人走就比较容易。这是一种思维捷径，能帮我们应对不确定的时候，或者快速做选择。我们从很小就开始这样做了。跟着父母……有些人是跟着老师，就是那些帮我们学习、帮我们理解世界的人。有些企业就会利用这一点，比如通过代言：牙医推荐牙膏，运动员代言运动服。

Pippa：Ben says that endorsements代言 work as a mental shortcut思维捷径. This is something that helps us make a decision quickly. If we trust the endorsement代言, then we don't need to think about it that much.

Pippa：本说代言起到思维捷径的作用。思维捷径就是帮我们快速做决定的东西。如果我们信任代言人，就不用想太多了。

Phil：In this episode, we're going to look at the way that people can be convinced说服，使相信 to do things.

Phil：这一集我们要看看人们是怎样被说服去做某些事的。

Pippa：And as usual, we'll learn some useful new words and phrases. And remember, you'll find all the vocabulary and a quiz on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

Pippa：和往常一样，我们会学一些有用的新单词和短语。记得在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上可以找到全部词汇和小测验。

Phil：OK. But first I have a question for you, Pippa. Today we're talking about behavioural行为的 science. What's the name of the theory that says people respond to small prompts提示? Is it:
a) push theory,
b) pull theory, or c) nudge轻推，助推 theory?

Phil：好。不过先问你一个问题，皮帕。今天我们聊行为科学。有一种理论说人会对小小的提示做出反应，它叫什么？是 a) 推理论，b) 拉理论，还是 c) 助推理论？

Pippa：Oh, I'm not sure. I'm going to say
b) pull theory.

Pippa：哦，我不确定。我选 b) 拉理论。

Phil：OK. Well, we'll find out弄清楚，得知 the answer at the end of the programme. In recent years, many fast-food chains快餐连锁店 have installed touchscreen触摸屏 machines for people to order their food. They've reported taking more money as a result. Could behavioural行为的 science tell us why this happens? Here's product designer Dean Ward speaking to BBC World Service's Business Daily.

Phil：好，节目最后揭晓答案。近几年很多快餐连锁店都装了触屏点餐机让顾客点餐。他们说营业额因此增加了。行为科学能解释为什么吗？我们听听产品设计师迪恩·沃德在 BBC 国际频道《每日商业》里怎么说。

Dean Ward：Firstly, the psychology心理 of speaking to someone and feeling judged觉得被评判 – we think is a key factor因素. So, would you like extra fries? Would you like to go large换大份? Not all people, but I think there's definitely a large proportion of很大一部分 people who may feel judged觉得被评判 in those instances情况，场合 and may say no. There's the fact that you've got more time to look. You can see the product, you can see what's in it, you can see all the products linked to it as well. And also around upsell追加销售 as well. Would you like to add this? Would you like to do that? Because you've got more time and you're not being judged, you're very much more inclined倾向于……的 to actually say yes to these things. And that's typically what we're seeing – an increased basket spend客单价，单次消费额 of typically 25–30%.

Dean Ward：首先，跟人当面说话时怕被评判的心理，我们认为是一个关键因素。比如：要不要多加薯条？要不要换大份？不是所有人，但我觉得肯定有很大一部分人在这种时候会觉得被评判，于是说不要。还有一点是你有更多时间慢慢看。你能看到产品，看到里面有什么，还能看到所有相关的产品。另外还有追加销售：要不要加这个？要不要来那个？因为你时间更充裕，又没人评判你，你就更愿意说要。我们通常看到的就是这样：每单消费一般会增加 25% 到 30%。

Pippa：If people feel judged觉得被评判, then it means that they worry what other people will think of them. If we have to ask a human for extra fries, we might worry what they think of us, but no one feels judged觉得被评判 by a computer screen.

Pippa：感觉被评判，意思是担心别人会怎么看自己。如果要跟一个真人说多加薯条，我们可能会担心对方怎么看我们，但没人会觉得被电脑屏幕评判。

Phil：If you upsell追加销售 something, then you get someone to spend more. For example, waiters often try to get people to buy larger portions（食物的）一份, more drinks, or dessert.

Phil：追加销售，就是让别人多花钱。比如服务员常常想让顾客点大份、多点饮料或者点甜品。

Pippa：Dean says that upselling追加销售 can increase people's basket spend客单价，单次消费额. A basket spend客单价，单次消费额 is the total amount that someone spends in one transaction交易, on everything that's in their basket. Now, this is an example of a business using behavioural行为的 science to nudge轻推，助推 people to do things. But it's not just businesses that use behavioural行为的 science in this way. In Tunisia, the United Nations World Food Programme世界粮食计划署 wanted to encourage people to eat food together more often. They made a TV show set in a restaurant. Let's hear from Takwa Khelifi from the World Food Programme世界粮食计划署, talking to BBC World Service's Business Daily.

Pippa：迪恩说追加销售能提高客单价。客单价就是一个人一次交易里买下篮子里所有东西花的总钱数。这是企业用行为科学轻轻推动人们去做事的例子。但不只企业会这样用行为科学。在突尼斯，联合国世界粮食计划署想鼓励人们更多地一起吃饭。他们拍了一部以餐厅为背景的电视剧。我们听听世界粮食计划署的塔克瓦·赫利菲在 BBC 国际频道《每日商业》里怎么说。

Takwa Khelifi：So, we needed something really creative and really different to think outside of the box跳出框框思考, or to let people see themselves in those stories, because people are learning and changing by imitating模仿 and modelling示范行为（供人模仿） and, like, observing others' behaviours and others' actions and emotional reactions to things. So, this is why we tried this project or this... tried this product or this TV series – in order that you impact影响 people.

Takwa Khelifi：所以我们需要一些真正有创意、与众不同的东西，跳出常规去思考，让人们在这些故事里看到自己，因为人是通过模仿、效仿，还有观察别人的行为、行动以及对事情的情绪反应来学习和改变的。这就是我们尝试这个项目，或者说这个产品、这部电视剧的原因：为了影响人们。

Phil：Takwa says that they needed to think outside the box跳出框框思考. This means to try and think in a different way, to come up with想出 something creative.

Phil：塔克瓦说他们需要跳出框框思考。意思是试着换个方式想问题，想出有创意的点子。

Pippa：The TV programme leads to people modelling示范行为（供人模仿） behaviour. If you model behaviour示范行为, then you behave in a way that other people can copy. Now Phil, I think it's time to hear the answer to your question.

Pippa：这部电视节目让人们去示范行为。示范行为，就是你的做法可以让别人照着学。菲尔，我想该揭晓你那道题的答案了。

Phil：Yes, it is. I asked what theory says that people respond to small prompts提示 to change their behaviour.

Phil：是的。我问的是：哪种理论认为人会因为小小的提示而改变行为。

Pippa：I thought it was pull theory...

Pippa：我以为是拉理论……

Phil：...which I'm afraid was the wrong answer. Nudge轻推，助推 theory says that people's behaviour can be changed by small prompts提示 or nudges轻推，助推.

Phil：……恐怕答错了。助推理论认为，人的行为可以被小小的提示或推动所改变。

Pippa：OK. Let's recap回顾 the vocabulary we've learned, starting with mental shortcut思维捷径, which is something that helps us make a decision quickly, usually because we don't need to think about it.

Pippa：好。我们来回顾一下学过的词汇，先是 mental shortcut（思维捷径），就是帮我们快速做决定的东西，通常是因为我们不用多想。

Phil：If someone feels judged觉得被评判, then they're worried about what other people think about them.

Phil：如果有人 feels judged（觉得被评判），就是担心别人怎么看自己。

Pippa：Upsell追加销售 refers to persuading someone to buy something extra, like a dessert at a restaurant.

Pippa：Upsell（追加销售）指说服别人多买点东西，比如在餐厅里多点一份甜品。

Phil：Basket spend客单价，单次消费额 is what you spend in one transaction交易 on the things in your shopping basket.

Phil：Basket spend（客单价）是你一次交易里为购物篮里的东西花的钱。

Pippa：If you think outside the box跳出框框思考, then you think about something in a different way to come up with想出 a creative solution.

Pippa：Think outside the box（跳出框框思考）就是换一种方式想问题，想出有创意的解决办法。

Phil：And finally, modelling示范行为（供人模仿） is behaving in a way that others can copy. Once again, our six minutes are up, but why not head over to去，前往 our website, bbclearningenglish.com, to try the quiz and worksheet练习题 for this episode. See you again soon!

Phil：最后，modelling（示范）就是用一种别人可以照着学的方式去做。六分钟又到了，不妨去我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 做做这一集的小测验和练习题。下次见！

Pippa：Bye!

Pippa：再见！

过关标准：不看原文能用中文说出这集讲了什么（代言为什么管用、触屏点餐为什么让人多花钱、突尼斯电视剧的目的），6 个表达都知道意思，Dean 那段能流利读下来。

小练习

  1. Choosing the brand you already know is a mental ______.（捷径）
  2. I don't like asking questions in class because I feel ______.（被评判）
  3. The waiter tried to ______ us a bottle of expensive wine.（追加销售）
  4. We need a creative idea, so let's think outside the ______.（框框）
  5. Parents should ______ good behaviour for their children.（示范）
  6. Most people trust experts who seem ______ and knowledgeable.（可信的）
点开看答案

开头那题选 c，nudge theory，助推理论。皮帕猜的是 pull theory，猜错了。触屏点餐后每单消费一般增加 25% 到 30%；电视剧是在突尼斯拍的。填空：1. shortcut 2. judged 3. upsell 4. box 5. model 6. credible

今天的小思考（为口语 Part 3 和大作文做准备）：Do you think advertising does more harm than good? 用英语说两三句：I think adverts can be useful because ... / However, some adverts persuade people to buy things they don't need, so ...。也可以想想：你最近一次冲动消费是什么？是不是被广告或名人推荐影响了？
